context: A ~30 minute engineering architecture review for 'Raven', a product that records meetings, transcribes them, and lets you ask questions across your meeting history. The team is hardening the design before a build sprint.

mustInclude: Sarah says today's review covers four areas: authentication, the database, the transcription pipeline, and deployment.
Light banter about a previous late deploy before getting down to business.
Final decision: refresh tokens are stored in httpOnly cookies, NOT in localStorage. This supersedes the earlier localStorage idea.
JWT access tokens expire after 15 minutes.
They will add refresh token rotation: each refresh token is one-time use, and detecting a reused token revokes the whole session.
Decision: rate-limit the login endpoint to 5 requests per minute per IP, specifically to stop credential stuffing attacks.
Action item: Jordan will write the authentication threat model document by Friday.
Decision: Postgres is the primary database, chosen for relational integrity which matters for billing.
Decision: use the pgvector extension on Postgres for the meeting-memory embeddings instead of a separate vector database.
Redis is used for caching and as the BullMQ job queue, not as a primary datastore.
Action item: Alex will benchmark pgvector HNSW versus IVFFlat indexes next week.
Deepgram stays the transcription provider, picked earlier for sub-second latency and built-in diarization.
Decision: defer speaker diarization to a v4 batch job, because running it as a batch job is cheaper than doing it live.
Risk discussed: the Deepgram transcript clock can drift from the recording clock, and if the offset is wrong every citation clip links to the wrong moment.
Action item: Sam will verify the transcript-to-recording time offset and store it per meeting.
Decision: deploy on Fly.io in a single region, us-east, to start.
Decision: add structured JSON logging now, but defer full distributed tracing with Langfuse until the eval loop actually needs it.
Action item: Priya will draft the Q3 roadmap by the end of the week.
Sarah recaps that the big decisions were httpOnly refresh tokens, Postgres with pgvector, deferring diarization, and deploying on Fly.io.
They agree to sync again next week.
